boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten Harvard spaces for quiet work, group projects, media making, mending, conversation, and breaks between classes.

cards.entity_name: Smith Campus Center 10th Floor Riverview Commons
cards.title: Take the Long View
cards.subtitle: Affiliate study space above Harvard Square
cards.notes: Bring reading for an unhurried session, then use the windows for a visual reset; carry your Harvard ID because this floor is affiliate-only.
cards.short_summary: A high-floor commons where students can pair relaxed study with broad campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard identifies the Smith Campus Center's 10th floor as a student study space with elevated views; its campus guide says areas beyond the public Welcome Pavilion and Arcade require Harvard ID.
cards.access_notes: The 10th floor requires a valid Harvard University ID; confirm building access and term hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Cabot Science Library Open Collaborative Areas
cards.title: Work Where Talking Fits
cards.subtitle: Collaborative seating in the Science Center
cards.notes: Use the main or lower level when a project needs conversation; choose the second floor instead when the group separates for quiet work.
cards.short_summary: Flexible Cabot seating supports discussion without sending every team into a reservable room.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Library says Cabot's main and lower levels provide varied seating for quiet and collaborative work, while its second floor has quiet-study desks and carrels.
cards.access_notes: Library access and staffed hours vary by date; consult the live hours shown on Harvard Library's Cabot page.

cards.title: Repair It Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Shared mending equipment inside Cabot
cards.notes: Bring a small repair or simple textile project; review equipment guidance first and ask about training if you have not used the machines before.
cards.short_summary: A practical shared station turns a library stop into time for mending and simple textile work.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Library states that Cabot's Sewing Station provides sewing machines, tools, and basic supplies for mending and simple textile projects, with training available.
cards.access_notes: The station is inside Cabot Science Library; verify library access and equipment availability before arriving.

cards.title: Commit to Complete Silence
cards.subtitle: Silent study inside Widener Library
cards.notes: Choose Loker when you can work without conversation; silence devices and prepare materials before sitting so you do not interrupt the room.
cards.short_summary: Widener's explicitly silent reading room is suited to work that benefits from minimal interruption.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Library describes the Loker Reading Room as a silent study space inside Widener Library and shows students working at its desks.
cards.access_notes: Widener access is controlled by Harvard Library policies; check current hours and bring the credentials required for entry.

cards.title: Share a Skylit Table
cards.subtitle: Quiet four-seat desks in Widener
cards.notes: Settle at a four-person desk for quiet parallel work, and use the comfortable seating when you need a short break from the page or screen.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled room offers shared tables without turning quiet study into group discussion.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Library describes Phillips Reading Room as a quiet, light-filled open space with four-person desks and comfortable break seating.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Widener Library; current building hours and Harvard Library entry requirements apply.

cards.title: Pick Your Silent-Study Setup
cards.subtitle: Tables, powered carrels, and soft seating at Lamont
cards.notes: Match the seat to the task: use an outlet-equipped carrel for laptop work, a table for spreading out, or soft seating for sustained reading.
cards.short_summary: One silent room provides several seating modes, including carrels equipped with outlet strips.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Library calls Donatelli Reading Room a light-filled silent-study space with tables, outlet-equipped carrels, and soft seating.
cards.access_notes: Lamont is open to Harvard students, faculty, and staff; check the live schedule because displayed hours vary by date.

cards.title: Mix Work With Conversation
cards.subtitle: Social study seating inside Lamont Library
cards.notes: Use a table or armchair when conversation is part of the plan; the desktop computers can handle a quick research or printing task.
cards.short_summary: Lamont's café supports social study and offers desktop computers for brief research and printing.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Library says Lamont Café has tables, armchairs, and desktop computers and is used for studying, socializing, quick research, and printing.
cards.access_notes: The café is within Lamont, which is restricted to Harvard students, faculty, and staff; verify current hours.

cards.title: Read Above Harvard Yard
cards.subtitle: Collection study and soft seating in Lamont
cards.notes: Bring poetry-related research or ordinary coursework; use the group tables for materials and the soft seats for reading beside the Yard view.
cards.short_summary: This collection room welcomes both poetry researchers and students seeking a comfortable place to study.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Library says the Woodberry Poetry Room offers group tables and soft seating overlooking Harvard Yard and welcomes collection users and general studying.
cards.access_notes: Located on Lamont's third floor; Harvard-affiliate building access and current library hours apply.

cards.title: Study Among Music Collections
cards.subtitle: Open seating in Loeb Music Library
cards.notes: Choose a desk for focused work or an armchair for reading, and keep collaboration quiet enough to respect others using the open room.
cards.short_summary: An identifiable Loeb study room combines desks, soft chairs, and nearby music-library collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Library lists the Loeb Spalding Room as a second-floor open study space with couches or armchairs and private desks.
cards.access_notes: Loeb is open to Harvard ID holders; visitors seeking general collections must apply for access. Check current hours.

cards.title: Pause, Cook, or Connect
cards.subtitle: Student commons beneath Memorial Church
cards.notes: Enter opposite Canaday Hall for a between-class reset; use the lounge to study, meet classmates, or prepare food in the shared kitchen.
cards.short_summary: A Harvard-student commons brings study, conversation, relaxation, and a kitchen into one ground-level space.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Church says current Harvard students may use the ground-level Student Oasis during the academic year to relax, study, cook, and connect with friends.
cards.access_notes: Available to current Harvard students during the academic year; use the entrance opposite Canaday Hall and confirm term hours.
